Protected view

No install. The photo is a short video encrypted with Common Encryption; the browser's own DRM decrypts it inside the device's protected path (Widevine in Chrome and Edge, PlayReady as a fallback in Edge on Windows, FairPlay on Apple devices). The photo is shown only with protection this page accepts: hardware protection on any device, and software protection in Chrome and Edge on Windows and Android (screenshots under software protection were measured black in Chrome and Edge on a Windows PC and in Chrome on an Android phone, 2026-10-11). On other browsers and platforms, Apple devices included, the photo is held back until each is measured the same way. It starts on its own when the page opens; the buttons only run it again.

Apple's test, on this iPhone, iPad or Mac. The photo is held back here until a screenshot on this kind of device is measured black. Instead, the four short videos above play, none of them a CCS picture: three through Apple's protected path (FairPlay), namely Axinom's test film, our test card, and our test card licensed by our own Axinom account as a picture would be; and the film unprotected, as a control.

  1. Wait until they are moving (about ten seconds), and scroll so that all four videos and the line under each are on the screen.
  2. Take a screenshot (press the side or top button together with volume up, or with the Home button on a model that has one; on a Mac, Shift-Command-3), and a screen recording if you can.
  3. Open the screenshot in Photos. The protected ones should be black; the control should show the film. A black one counts only if the line under it says playing with a size (for example 720x960) and its time moving; if it says no frame, nothing was playing there, and if the control is black too, the screenshot proves nothing on this device.

Apple's test, what happened, in order


  
The film is Tears of Steel by the Blender Foundation (CC BY 3.0), from Axinom's public test streams. The protected videos are licensed by Axinom's FairPlay licence service with Axinom's evaluation FairPlay certificate, issued by Apple: the film under Axinom's own packaging, the card under ours (tools/fairplay-card.mjs). The card's first form uses Axinom's public test key, which Axinom's public licence token unlocks; its second uses a key of its own, whose token our account made.
